The idea A fast, inexpensive model looks at something Trov already holds — a feed entry, a ticket, a proposal, an item in Unplaced — and attaches a small structured judgement to it: a priority, a category, a tag, a destination, a risk. That is what makes it cheap, and what makes it safe to use in many places.

request.state:
A doc an agent wrote: “Guided repository setup: the owner's decision”.

The agent filed it under “rulings”.

Decision (owner, 2026-10-10) Trov does not work out how a repository is hosted by reading it. It asks. When someone sets up a repository in an organization they get a short guided setup: they say what the stack is, and Trov then connects each piece with them, telling them exactly where to get each key as they go. At the end the Repo dashboard is the one that fits what they said. This settles the open question in 147 for the first version: no file is opened, and no model is needed to know the stack. Detection from events Trov already captures (the hosting branch's "Detected: Vercel") only PRE-FILLS an answer; the person confirms it.

A doc an agent wrote: “Server-side AI: the decided build”.

The agent filed it under “specs”.

Server-side AI: the decided build (2026-10-15) Decided. This is the design of Trov handoff 10 (claimed 2026-10-15), built into PR 178 on . Updated 2026-10-15 after merging with 185 (hosting providers): migrations moved to 0058–0067, and hosting deploys feed the router and repo state. Where (the older background spec) disagrees, this file wins. What was verified before building, and the migration numbers, are in . How the system works One loop: capture → route → decide → write → show → learn. 1. Capture already exists: the GitHub webhook and reconcile, plus the app's writers. 2. Route is plain code. Each write marks the scopes it made stale. No model is involved. 3. The AI pass in the cron works through stale scopes per org, within the switch, the allowance and the cron budget. 4. Jev decides; Haiku writes. - Jev (TypeSafe, about $0.0001 a check) answers classifications and gates: is this worth a Haiku call? - Haiku 5.5 writes words, only past a gate, and reads item cards, never raw PR bodies or commit lists. 5. Store everything as computed rows. Screens, MCP, emails and Ask Trov all read those rows. Nothing calls a model while a page loads. 6. Learn. Accept, Dismiss and "Wrong?" go
